Good news: this machine already has the secure setup in place. The global Git config (`C:/Program Files/Git/etc/gitconfig`) has `credential.helper=manager`, which is Git Credential Manager (GCM 2.5.0, confirmed installed at `C:\Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git-credential-manager.exe`). That's the right tool for this — it caches credentials securely via Windows' native credential store (DPAPI-backed) and handles token refresh automatically, so once you authenticate one time per remote, you won't be prompted again. It also already has `usehttppath=true` for `dev.azure.com`, suggesting Azure DevOps has been used here before.

I'd avoid the alternative some guides suggest (`git config credential.helper store`) — that writes your password/token in **plaintext** to `~/.git-credentials` on disk, which isn't something I'd set up for you.

One thing I can't do without more info: this sandbox repo has **no remotes configured at all** (`git remote -v` is empty), so there's no "internal" remote for me to point at. What's the URL for the internal remote (e.g. `https://dev.azure.com/...` or an internal Git server URL)? Once you give me that, I'll:
1. `git remote add origin <url>`
2. Trigger one `git push` so GCM prompts you once, stores the credential securely, and every push after that is silent.

If it's a self-hosted server (not GitHub/Azure DevOps/GitLab), let me know the host too — GCM may need `credential.<url>.provider=generic` or an SSH key setup instead, depending on what auth it supports.
